text:
maya-support: Hey team, customer (acme-inc) reporting intermittent 403s on SSO post-idp cert rotation around 2025-11-02T12:03Z. They say some users can login, others get 403 when POSTing SAMLResponse. Root cause seems timing-related.

maya-support: Example error from our logs: `SAMLValidator: recipient mismatch 'https://app.redwood.com/sso/acs' != 'https://app.redwood.com/saml/acs'` and `Signature verification failed` for a subset of requests.

liam-eng-sre: Thanks — can you dump the raw SAMLResponse for a failing request (base64) and the RelayState they sent? Also, has IdP announced metadata URL change or returned a 302 during their rotation?

maya-support: Pasted minimal repro (sanitized):
```
POST /saml/acs HTTP/1.1
Host: app.redwood.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

SAMLResponse=PHNhbWwy..(base64)..D4=&RelayState=acme-session-123
```
We see failures from 12:05–12:20 UTC, then occasional successes after 12:22. IdP confirmed they rotated signing certs and updated metadata at https://idp.acme.com/metadata.xml at 12:03, and they use an aggressive CDN that returns 302 -> origin during rotation.

dinesh-support: I decoded one of the failing SAMLResponses locally. Assertion Subject/Recipient points to `https://app.redwood.com/sso/acs` (no trailing /), but our ACS in the relying-party config is `https://app.redwood.com/saml/acs`. Customer says they didn't change ACS.

dinesh-support: Also noticed the <KeyDescriptor> elements in their metadata are reversed order during the rotation window (signing key appears after encryption key) — our metadata parser expects signing key first in some codepaths.

olivia-oncall: deploy-bot shows a metadata fetch at 12:04 that got `302 Found` then a 200 with gzipped payload at 12:05. There was a retry backoff that skipped validation for a short window, leaving an older cached metadata without the new signing key. This could explain the intermittent signature verification failures.

liam-eng-sre: Bingo — sounds like a metadata polling + cache window race. Two issues we should address:
- accept either KeyDescriptor ordering when picking signing key (defensive)
- make polling treat 302->200 as a successful atomic swap or apply short grace period after metadata change to accept both old/new certs

liam-eng-sre: Can you provide a failing request id and server log tail for one time range? Need exact request id to correlate with metadata fetch events.

maya-support: Request id 8fa3b2c1, logs below: 
```
[2025-11-02T12:07:08Z] req=8fa3b2c1 POST /saml/acs 403 "Signature verification failed"
[2025-11-02T12:07:08Z] debug: SAML signed with key thumbprint=AB:34:... expected signing key thumbprint=CD:56:...
[2025-11-02T12:07:09Z] metadata-poller: fetched https://idp.acme.com/metadata.xml status=302 -> 200 size=8.7KB gzipped
[2025-11-02T12:07:10Z] metadata-cache: swapped metadata (old->new) but parsing used encryption key first
```

olivia-oncall: I've promoted this to P1 for oncall. Quick mitigation for customer: add their alternate ACS (`/sso/acs`) to our relying-party allowed recipients list for acme-inc while we patch. That will stop 403s immediately. They can also temporarily push metadata to origin without 302s.

dinesh-support: Repro steps for folks:
1) Get SAMLResponse from customer (base64).
2) curl -v -X POST -d "SAMLResponse=<base64>&RelayState=..." -H "Host: app.redwood.com" "https://app.redwood.com/saml/acs"
3) tail -f /var/log/redwood/sso.log and watch for req id errors.

liam-eng-sre: Proposed patch: loosen KeyDescriptor selection to pick element where `use="signing"` OR inspect KeyInfo to find RSA public exponent/signing properties. Also, add 30s grace window around metadata swaps where both old and new signing keys are accepted. I opened a draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987 (wip).

olivia-oncall: Can we push a hotfix config to prod to accept alternate ACS for acme-inc now? I can do a fast rollback if anything breaks.

maya-support: Customer approved the temporary ACS add. I patched relying-party for acme-inc to accept both `/saml/acs` and `/sso/acs`. Monitoring shows successful logins immediately after. :thumbsup:

liam-eng-sre: Thanks — I'll continue with the robust fix. Tests to add: metadata sequence reorder, gzipped-302 ingestion, and a poller unit test ensuring we treat 302->200 as a single update event.

dinesh-support: Note for runbook: when customer rotates certs, recommend they: 1) upload new metadata early, 2) avoid CDN-level 302s during propagation, or 3) provide a pinned fingerprint in support ticket for emergency acceptance. We'll add guidance to SSO onboards.

olivia-oncall: Filed incident doc and postmortem placeholder. Assigning liam-eng-sre for patch, dinesh-support for runbook updates. I'll follow up in eng-sre channel when PR is ready to merge. :eyes:

maya-support: Closing loop with customer — they've verified logins and will keep us posted if anything recurs. Thanks all.
